lesson.menu_title: She Said She Would Call — Passing On Questions and Requests
lesson.menu_desc: Reported questions and requests, for the voicemails and emails waiting when you come back -- 37 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- She Said She Would Call
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 12 -- She Said She Would Call

listenings.text: Hi Rosa, this is Diego Ferraz from the mining account. It is Tuesday, about ten in the morning, and I am sorry to leave three things on a voicemail. First, our finance director wants to know whether the new fare includes two bags or only one, because the team always travels with equipment. Second, could you tell me when the contract will be ready? Our legal department asks me about it every single day. And third, please do not send another reminder about the March invoice. It was paid on Friday, and I have the confirmation here in front of me. Call me back before noon on Thursday if you can, because after that I am on a plane to Santiago.

When a client leaves you a question, your job is not only to answer it. It is to pass it on so precisely that a colleague could answer it without calling the client again. That means keeping the question as a question. Not Diego called about the bags, but Diego asked whether the new fare included two bags. Requests work in exactly the same way. If somebody asked you to do something, write down who asked, what they asked for, and by when. And if somebody told you not to do something, write that down first, because it is the message your colleague is most likely to get wrong. Finally, reply on the same day, even when you do not have the answer yet. A short message that acknowledges the request and gives a date is professional. Silence is not.

paras: Come back from three days on the road and you will find what every account manager finds: seven voicemails, forty emails, and a colleague who covered for you with a page of notes. Almost none of it is a statement. It is questions and requests. One client asked whether the fare included two bags, another wanted to know when the contract would be ready, and a third asked you to call him back before noon.

The way you pass those messages on to your team decides whether anything gets done. The weak version is a summary: Diego called about the contract. The useful version keeps the question: Diego asked when the contract would be ready, and whether we could move the signing to the twentieth. The second sentence can be answered by anybody on the team. The first one only creates another phone call.

Requests deserve the same care. If a client told you not to send another reminder, write exactly that, because the next colleague who chases him up will damage a relationship you spent years building. If he asked you to loop in his finance team, say who asked, and by when.

There is one more habit, and it separates the professionals from everybody else. When a question is unclear, they do not guess. They reply on the same day, acknowledge the message, and ask the client to clarify. A two-line email that says you received the inquiry and will get back to him on Thursday is worth more than a perfect answer that arrives a week late.

Passing on clients' questions and requests accurately, so the team can act on them

items: The column says most of what is waiting after a trip is statements.

items.situation: A client asked if the new fare included two bags. Pass the question on to your team.
tips: Yes or no question: use if or whether
She asked whether the new fare included two bags

items.situation: Your manager wants to know what the client asked about the contract date.
tips: Keep when, then normal word order
He asked when the contract would be ready

items.situation: A colleague asks what the bank's travel manager wanted you to do.
tips: A request takes asked me to plus the base verb
She asked me to loop in her finance team

items.situation: You have to warn a colleague about something the client does not want.
tips: He told me not to send another reminder

items.situation: A client asked where you had sent the proposal, and you are reporting it.
tips: No did in a reported question
She asked where I had sent the proposal

items.situation: A client's question was not clear. Tell your manager what you did about it.
tips: I acknowledged it and asked him to clarify the dates

extra_audio.text: Julio welcomes Rosa back and tells her that there are three messages that cannot wait. He explains that Diego asked whether the new fare included two bags and wanted to know when the contract would be ready. He adds that Diego asked Rosa to call him back before noon on Thursday and told him not to send another reminder. Julio admits that he was the person who chased Diego up the last time. Rosa decides to call Diego first and to ask the bank's travel manager to clarify which finance team she means.
